add.text: A superchron is a polarity interval lasting at least 10 million years.
The name Kiaman comes from the Australian town of Kiama, where some of the first geological evidence of the superchron was found in 1925.
A possible Ordovician superchron has so far been found only in the Moyero river section north of the polar circle in Siberia.
At Mazon Creek, chemicals released by decaying soft tissue changed the surrounding sediment into a siderite concretion that encased the fossil.
The Kasimovian boundary covers a time of globally low sea level, which left disconformities in many sequences of this age.
The glaciation ended suddenly as a rapid rise in CO2 to about 600 ppm brought a warmer climate.
Diapsids are true reptiles, and the common ancestor of all living reptiles was almost certainly a diapsid.
Reptiles went through a major evolutionary radiation in response to the drier climate that came before the rainforest collapse.
Amphibians, then the dominant vertebrates, fared poorly in the rainforest collapse, while reptiles kept diversifying thanks to the hard-shelled egg and scales, which hold water better.
Ancylopoda are browsing, herbivorous perissodactyl mammals with long, curved, cleft claws.
Morphological evidence indicates the Ancylopoda diverged from the tapirs, rhinoceroses and horses after the Brontotheria.
The Mata Menge teeth are similar in size and shape to those of H. floresiensis but more primitive.
The Mata Menge hominins likely arose from insular dwarfism acting on Homo erectus.
West African groups such as the Yoruba and Mende carry the archaic DNA, which shows it was acquired long before agriculture spread.
The Rockland tephra could be the most voluminous eruption in the Cascade Volcanic Arc, nearly twice the size of the Mazama ash.
From 600,000 to 400,000 years ago, eruptions built the large conical stratovolcano Mount Tehama.
The Great Barrier Reef is the world's largest coral reef system, made of over 2,900 individual reefs and 900 islands.
Ribbon reefs and deltaic reefs form only in the northern part of the Great Barrier Reef.
Ursine bears originated around five million years ago, with extensive hybridization among the different species.
The founding population of most North American brown bears arrived first, with its genetic lineage developing around 177,000 years ago.
The mammoth steppe, also called steppe-tundra, was once the Earth's most extensive biome.
The mammoth steppe was cold and dry and relatively featureless, though climate, topography and geography varied considerably.
Its fauna was dominated by reindeer, muskox, saiga antelope, steppe bison, horses, woolly rhinoceros and woolly mammoth.
The Clactonian dates to the early Hoxnian Interglacial, around 424-415,000 years ago.
The Clactonian differs from the contemporaneous Acheulean mainly in not using handaxes; thick irregular flakes struck from a flint core served as choppers.
The distinctiveness of the Clactonian has been questioned, because its techniques resemble the Acheulean and handaxes occur in Britain both before and after it.
It is widely agreed that the grey wolf lineage goes back 2 million years to Canis etruscus, followed in the Middle Pleistocene by Canis mosbachensis.

A 2010 study found that Canis diversity fell by the end of the Early to Middle Pleistocene, leaving in Eurasia the small C. mosbachensis-C. variabilis wolves and the large hypercarnivorous Canis (Xenocyon) lycanoides.
Estimates of when polar bears split from brown bears differ: a 2010 study gave about 150,000 years ago and a 2012 study about 600,000 years ago.
Glaciation events over hundreds of thousands of years led to the origin of polar bears and to their later interactions and hybridizations with brown bears.
Mesotherium was a long-lived, superficially rodent-like, burrowing notoungulate from South America.
Mesotherium was the largest typothere, possibly weighing up to 100 kg.
Karymsky is an active stratovolcano on the Kamchatka Peninsula in Russia.
Homo sapiens seems to have reached the western Sahelian zone by 130,000 years ago.
Early modern human expansion in sub-Saharan Africa appears to have contributed to the end of late Acheulean (Fauresmith) industries about 130,000 years ago.
Burial and ritual are among the religious behaviors people began to show in the Middle or Upper Paleolithic, alongside art.
Some scientists propose that Middle Paleolithic societies such as the Neanderthals may also have practiced the earliest totemism or animal worship, besides burying their dead.
Dromaeosaur body fossils are known from the Early Cretaceous (145-140 million years ago) and the family survived until the Maastrichtian, 66 Ma.
Dromaeosaurs belong to Coelurosauria, in the clade Paraves, together with avialans and troodontids.
With the spinosaurids, carcharodontosaurids were the largest predators of the early and middle Cretaceous throughout Gondwana, with species also in North America, Europe and possibly Asia.
Acrocanthosaurus, Giganotosaurus, Mapusaurus, Carcharodontosaurus and Tyrannotitan all rivaled Tyrannosaurus and Spinosaurus in size.
The sea flooded large parts of what is now Queensland and Central Australia at least four times during the early Cretaceous.
The present-day Winton Formation represents remnants of the river plains that filled the basin the Eromanga Sea left behind.
In 2006 Swedish geologists found indications of a tsunami flooding the Swedish southern coast about 145 million years ago, speculated to be associated with the Mjolnir impact.
The orb-web consists of a frame and supporting radii overlaid with a sticky capture spiral.
Because orb-webs absorb the impact of flying prey, orbicularian spiders became the dominant predators of aerial insects in many ecosystems.
The Faraoni Thermal Excursion was a hyperthermal event of the Hauterivian induced by flood basalt volcanism.
Anglerfish are ray-finned fish of the order Lophiiformes.
The earliest anglerfish fossils are from the Eocene of the Monte Bolca formation in Italy, and already show diversification into the modern families.
The Paja Formation dates from the late Hauterivian to the late Aptian.
The Selli event of the early Aptian, about 120 Ma, was active while the black shales of the Paja Formation were being deposited.
The impact occurred during deposition of the Cadna-owie Formation, whose age is estimated variously at 123-133 Ma or 115-112 Ma.
Tookoonooka is associated with several small oil fields.
Microbial mats may be responsible for preserving the soft tissue in many Las Hoyas fossils, such as the crest of Pelecanimimus.
Charophyte and ostracod assemblages constrain the age of Las Hoyas to the Late Barremian.
The Cretaceous Resinous Interval began roughly 125 million years ago, during the Barremian age.
After the interval, in the Maastrichtian, amber was widely distributed but scarce and rarely held bioinclusions.
Thalattosuchia is a clade of mostly marine crocodylomorphs that lived from the Early Jurassic to the Early Cretaceous and had a cosmopolitan distribution.
Thalattosuchians are not members of Crocodilia, and records from Thailand and China suggest some lived in freshwater.

The only Mesozoic monotremes come from Australia plus Patagonia; Teinolophos is dated Barremian, 126 Ma, and the many Cenomanian forms suggest monotremes were diversifying by the early Late Cretaceous.
One hypothesis is that monotremes arose in Australia in the Late Jurassic or Early Cretaceous and some migrated across the Antarctic land bridge to South America.
A Kayentatherium specimen shows that tritylodontids already had a marsupial-like reproductive style but produced much larger litters, around 38 perinates or possibly eggs.
Only two groups of non-mammaliaform cynodonts survived past the end of the Triassic, both in Probainognathia.
